notes: Reasoning Ability topic package 1 (Linear Seating, Circular Seating, Floor-Based and Box-Based Puzzles) of BATCH_010: 55 original questions built by tools/packages/REAS_pkg1.py. New puzzle structures (checked against every earlier REAS part file). Every puzzle is brute-forced to exactly one arrangement and every answer is read off it in code. All questions await human review.

stimuli.title: Twelve persons in two facing rows of six
stimuli.content:
Twelve persons Arya, Bhola, Chanda, Dhiren, Gulab, Hasan, Kapil, Lalit, Mohan, Nayan, Ravi and Tulsi sit in two parallel rows of six seats each. The persons in Row 1 face south and those in Row 2 face north, so each person faces exactly one person of the other row. (Facing south, the right is towards the west; facing north, the right is towards the east.)

- Mohan sits in Row 1, third from the east end of that row.
- Hasan faces Mohan, and Bhola sits immediately to the right of Hasan.
- Tulsi sits immediately to the right of Mohan, and Dhiren faces Tulsi.
- Ravi sits second to the left of Mohan, and Gulab sits between Mohan and Ravi.
- Lalit faces Ravi, and Chanda sits at one end of Row 2.
- Nayan faces Arya, who sits in the row that faces south.
stimuli.solution:
Number the columns 1 to 6 from the west in both rows.
Step 1: Mohan = Row 1, column 4. Hasan faces him: Row 2, column 4; Bhola, to Hasan's right (east): Row 2, column 5.
Step 2: Tulsi, to Mohan's right (west): Row 1, column 3; Dhiren faces her: Row 2, column 3.
Step 3: Ravi, second to Mohan's left (east): Row 1, column 6; Gulab between them: column 5. Lalit faces Ravi: Row 2, column 6, so Chanda is at the other end: Row 2, column 1.
Step 4: Free seats: Row 1 columns 1 and 2, Row 2 column 2. Nayan faces Arya, so they take the facing pair Row 2 column 2 and Row 1 column 2; Arya is in the south-facing Row 1, so Nayan is in Row 2, and Kapil gets Row 1, column 1.

| Column | Row 1 (facing south) | Row 2 (facing north) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Kapil | Chanda |
| 2 | Arya | Nayan |
| 3 | Tulsi | Dhiren |
| 4 | Mohan | Hasan |
| 5 | Gulab | Bhola |
| 6 | Ravi | Lalit |

stimuli.title: Ten seats, seven persons
stimuli.content:
Ten seats are placed in a straight row and numbered 1 to 10 from the left end. Seven persons Anvi, Bhim, Chiru, Dolu, Esha, Fuzail and Gita sit on seven of them, all facing north; the other three seats are vacant. Positions such as 'second to the right' count seats, including vacant ones.

- Anvi sits on seat 6, and Chiru sits immediately to the right of Anvi.
- Bhim sits at the extreme left end, and Dolu at the extreme right end.
- Fuzail sits immediately to the left of Dolu.
- Esha and Gita sit in adjacent seats, Esha to the left of Gita, and exactly one seat lies between Bhim and Esha.
stimuli.solution:
Step 1: Anvi = 6, Chiru = 7, Bhim = 1, Dolu = 10, Fuzail = 9.
Step 2: One seat lies between Bhim (1) and Esha: Esha = 3, and Gita, immediately to her right, = 4.
Step 3: The vacant seats are 2, 5 and 8.

| Seat | Person |
|---|---|
| 1 | Bhim |
| 2 | vacant |
| 3 | Esha |
| 4 | Gita |
| 5 | vacant |
| 6 | Anvi |
| 7 | Chiru |
| 8 | vacant |
| 9 | Fuzail |
| 10 | Dolu |

stimuli.title: Eight persons in a row, ranked by height
stimuli.content:
Eight persons Hiran, Ishu, Kuku, Lado, Mitu, Nanki, Pammi and Rinku sit in a straight row, all facing north. No two of them are of the same height. (Facing north, the right is towards the east.)

- Lado and Pammi sit at the two ends of the row, Lado at the left end.
- The tallest person sits immediately to the right of Lado, and the shortest person sits immediately to the right of the tallest person.
- Nanki is the second tallest and sits second to the right of the tallest person.
- Hiran sits second to the right of Nanki and is shorter than only Kuku and Nanki.
- Kuku is taller than Nanki.
- Ishu sits immediately to the left of Hiran, and Rinku immediately to the right of Hiran.
- Ishu is shorter than everyone except the shortest person; Rinku is taller than Lado, and Lado is taller than Pammi.
stimuli.solution:
Number the seats 1 to 8 from the left.
Step 1: Lado = 1, Pammi = 8. The tallest person is on seat 2 and the shortest on seat 3. Nanki (2nd tallest) = 4, Hiran (3rd tallest) = 6, Ishu = 5, Rinku = 7.
Step 2: Kuku and Mitu take seats 2 and 3. Kuku is taller than Nanki, the second tallest, so Kuku is the tallest (seat 2) and Mitu the shortest (seat 3).
Step 3: Ranks 4 to 7 remain for Ishu, Rinku, Lado and Pammi. Ishu is 7th; Rinku > Lado > Pammi in height: Rinku 4th, Lado 5th, Pammi 6th.

| Seat | Person | Height rank |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Lado | 5 |
| 2 | Kuku | 1 |
| 3 | Mitu | 8 |
| 4 | Nanki | 2 |
| 5 | Ishu | 7 |
| 6 | Hiran | 3 |
| 7 | Rinku | 4 |
| 8 | Pammi | 6 |

stimuli.title: Ten chairs, eight persons
stimuli.content:
Ten chairs are placed around a circular table, equally spaced. Eight persons Ajay, Bimal, Disha, Fateh, Jassi, Lucky, Rupal and Ujjal sit on eight of them, all facing the centre; two chairs are vacant. Positions such as 'second to the right' count chairs, including vacant ones. (Facing the centre, the right is anticlockwise.)

- Jassi sits opposite Ajay, and Bimal sits immediately to the left of Jassi.
- Rupal sits immediately to the right of Ajay. Fateh sits second to the right of Rupal, and the chair between Rupal and Fateh is vacant.
- Lucky sits immediately to the left of Ajay, and Disha sits immediately to the left of Lucky.
- Ujjal sits immediately to the right of Jassi.
- The two vacant chairs are exactly opposite each other.
stimuli.solution:
Number the chairs 0 to 9 anticlockwise from Ajay.
Step 1: Jassi = 5 (opposite), Bimal = 4 (Jassi's left, clockwise), Ujjal = 6.
Step 2: Rupal = 1, chair 2 is vacant, Fateh = 3.
Step 3: Lucky = 9, Disha = 8. The only chair left is 7, which is vacant — and it is exactly opposite chair 2, as required.

| Chair | Person |
|---|---|
| 0 | Ajay |
| 1 | Rupal |
| 2 | vacant |
| 3 | Fateh |
| 4 | Bimal |
| 5 | Jassi |
| 6 | Ujjal |
| 7 | vacant |
| 8 | Disha |
| 9 | Lucky |

stimuli.title: Seven persons facing in or out
stimuli.content:
Seven persons Rohit, Saloni, Tanuj, Urvi, Vedika, Xena and Yuvi sit around a circular table, equally spaced. Some of them face the centre and the others face outside. (Facing the centre, the right is anticlockwise; facing outside, it is clockwise.)

- Rohit faces the centre, and Urvi sits immediately to his right.
- Urvi faces outside, and Yuvi sits immediately to Urvi's left.
- Saloni sits immediately to the right of Yuvi, and the two of them face opposite directions.
- Vedika sits immediately to the left of Rohit and faces the same direction as Rohit.
- Tanuj sits immediately to the left of Vedika.
- Xena faces the centre, Xena and Tanuj face opposite directions, and Yuvi faces the same direction as Xena.
stimuli.solution:
Number the seats 0 to 6 anticlockwise from Rohit.
Step 1: Rohit faces the centre: Urvi = 1. Urvi faces outside, so her left is anticlockwise: Yuvi = 2.
Step 2: Vedika, on Rohit's left (clockwise), = 6 and faces the centre. Tanuj, on Vedika's left, = 5.
Step 3: Xena faces the centre; Yuvi faces the same way (centre), Tanuj the other way (outside). Saloni faces opposite to Yuvi (outside) and sits on Yuvi's right (anticlockwise): 3. Xena takes seat 4.

| Seat | Person | Facing |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Rohit | facing the centre |
| 1 | Urvi | facing outside |
| 2 | Yuvi | facing the centre |
| 3 | Saloni | facing outside |
| 4 | Xena | facing the centre |
| 5 | Tanuj | facing outside |
| 6 | Vedika | facing the centre |

stimuli.title: Six floors and six hobbies
stimuli.content:
Six persons Bablu, Chameli, Dinu, Ganesh, Heena and Jagan live on the six floors of a building, one on each floor (floor 1 is the lowermost, floor 6 the topmost). Each has a different hobby among Dancing, Painting, Reading, Singing, Swimming and Writing.

- Chameli lives on floor 4, Bablu immediately above her and Jagan immediately below her.
- Dinu lives on the topmost floor, and Heena lives below Ganesh.
- The person who likes Painting lives on an even-numbered floor between Jagan and Bablu.
- The person on the topmost floor likes Singing, and the person on floor 1 likes Reading.
- The person who likes Dancing lives immediately below the person who likes Painting.
- Bablu does not like Swimming.
stimuli.solution:
Step 1: Chameli = 4, Bablu = 5, Jagan = 3, Dinu = 6. Floors 1 and 2 remain; Heena is below Ganesh: Heena = 1, Ganesh = 2.
Step 2: Painting is on an even floor between 3 and 5: floor 4 (Chameli). Dancing is immediately below: floor 3 (Jagan). Singing: floor 6 (Dinu). Reading: floor 1 (Heena).
Step 3: Swimming and Writing remain for Ganesh and Bablu; Bablu does not swim: Bablu Writing, Ganesh Swimming.

| Floor | Person | Hobby |
|---|---|---|
| 6 | Dinu | Singing |
| 5 | Bablu | Writing |
| 4 | Chameli | Painting |
| 3 | Jagan | Dancing |
| 2 | Ganesh | Swimming |
| 1 | Heena | Reading |

stimuli.title: Two persons on each of four floors, with colours
stimuli.content:
Eight persons Arif, Chinki, Gudiya, Hanif, Lalu, Mamta, Pintu and Sweety live in a four-storey building, two persons on each floor (floor 1 is the lowermost, floor 4 the topmost). Each likes a different colour among Amber, Coral, Indigo, Lilac, Mint, Navy, Rose and Tan.

- Gudiya lives on floor 3 and likes Rose.
- Arif lives on the floor immediately above Gudiya's and likes Mint.
- Hanif lives on an even-numbered floor below Gudiya.
- Chinki and Mamta live on the same floor.
- Sweety lives above Lalu, and Pintu lives on the floor immediately below Lalu's.
- The person who likes Navy lives on the topmost floor. Hanif likes Amber and Pintu likes Lilac.
- The person who likes Tan lives on floor 3, and Chinki does not like Indigo.
stimuli.solution:
Step 1: Gudiya = 3 (Rose), Arif = 4 (Mint), Hanif = 2 (Amber).
Step 2: Chinki and Mamta share a floor; floors 2, 3 and 4 each have only one free place, so they live on floor 1.
Step 3: Lalu, Pintu and Sweety fill one place each on floors 2, 3 and 4. Pintu is immediately below Lalu and Sweety is above Lalu: Pintu = 2, Lalu = 3, Sweety = 4.
Step 4: Navy is on floor 4; Arif likes Mint, so Sweety likes Navy. Pintu likes Lilac. Tan is on floor 3, where Gudiya likes Rose, so Lalu likes Tan. Coral and Indigo remain for Chinki and Mamta; Chinki does not like Indigo: Chinki Coral, Mamta Indigo.

| Floor | Persons (colour) |
|---|---|
| 4 | Arif (Mint), Sweety (Navy) |
| 3 | Gudiya (Rose), Lalu (Tan) |
| 2 | Hanif (Amber), Pintu (Lilac) |
| 1 | Chinki (Coral), Mamta (Indigo) |

stimuli.title: A basement, a ground floor and six floors
stimuli.content:
A building has a basement, a ground floor and six floors above the ground floor (floors 1 to 6, floor 6 being the topmost). Eight persons Abhi, Barun, Chaya, Dilip, Emily, Feroz, Gagan and Harsha live in it, one on each of these eight levels. Each has a different profession among Actor, Baker, Cashier, Doctor, Editor, Farmer, Guard and Nurse. 'Level' means any of the eight (basement, ground floor or floor 1-6).

- Exactly three persons live above Emily, and Emily is the Actor.
- The Doctor lives two levels below Emily.
- Chaya lives on the ground floor, immediately above the Guard.
- Barun lives on the topmost floor, and Dilip lives two levels below Barun.
- Gagan lives between Dilip and Barun.
- Feroz lives below Harsha, and Abhi lives immediately above Harsha.
- The Nurse lives immediately above the Doctor.
- The Cashier lives immediately below the Editor, and the Editor lives below the Farmer.
stimuli.solution:
List the levels from the bottom: basement, ground, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6.
Step 1: Three persons live above Emily, so Emily is on floor 3 (the Actor). The Doctor is two levels lower: floor 1.
Step 2: Chaya = ground floor; the Guard is in the basement. Barun = floor 6, Dilip = floor 4, Gagan = floor 5.
Step 3: Feroz, Harsha and Abhi take the basement, floor 1 and floor 2. Abhi is immediately above Harsha and Feroz below Harsha: Feroz = basement (Guard), Harsha = floor 1 (Doctor), Abhi = floor 2.
Step 4: The Nurse is immediately above the Doctor: Abhi. Baker, Cashier, Editor and Farmer remain for Chaya (ground), Dilip (4), Gagan (5) and Barun (6). Cashier is immediately below Editor, and Editor is below Farmer: Cashier 4 (Dilip), Editor 5 (Gagan), Farmer 6 (Barun). Chaya is the Baker.

| Level | Person | Profession |
|---|---|---|
| floor 6 | Barun | Farmer |
| floor 5 | Gagan | Editor |
| floor 4 | Dilip | Cashier |
| floor 3 | Emily | Actor |
| floor 2 | Abhi | Nurse |
| floor 1 | Harsha | Doctor |
| the ground floor | Chaya | Baker |
| the basement | Feroz | Guard |

stimuli.title: Eight coloured boxes in a stack
stimuli.content:
Eight boxes A, C, E, H, K, N, R and W are kept one above another in a single stack (position 1 is the bottom and 8 the top). Each box is of a different colour among Aqua, Black, Cyan, Gold, Ivory, Lime, Plum and Rust.

- Box A is kept fourth from the bottom and is Black; Box N is kept immediately above Box A.
- Box K is kept at the top, and Box H is kept immediately below Box K.
- Box C is kept between Box N and Box H, and Box R is kept at the bottom.
- Box W is kept above Box E.
- The Ivory box is kept immediately above the Black box, and the top box is Cyan.
- The Gold box is kept two places below the Black box, and the Plum box is kept between the Gold and Black boxes.
- The Rust box is kept immediately below the Cyan box, and the bottom box is not Aqua.
stimuli.solution:
Step 1: A = 4 (Black), N = 5, K = 8, H = 7, C = 6, R = 1.
Step 2: Positions 2 and 3 remain for E and W; W is above E: E = 2, W = 3.
Step 3: Ivory = 5 (N), Cyan = 8 (K), Gold = 2 (E), Plum = 3 (W), Rust = 7 (H).
Step 4: Aqua and Lime remain for R (1) and C (6); the bottom box is not Aqua: R Lime, C Aqua.

| Position | Box | Colour |
|---|---|---|
| 8 | K | Cyan |
| 7 | H | Rust |
| 6 | C | Aqua |
| 5 | N | Ivory |
| 4 | A | Black |
| 3 | W | Plum |
| 2 | E | Gold |
| 1 | R | Lime |

stimuli.title: Eight boxes on two shelves
stimuli.content:
Eight boxes B, D, F, H, J, L, N and P are placed on two shelves, upper and lower, four boxes on each shelf in a line. Each box on the upper shelf is directly above one box on the lower shelf. Left and right are as seen from the front.

- Box J is on the upper shelf, third from the left, and Box F is directly below Box J.
- Box L is immediately to the right of Box F, and Box B is directly above Box L.
- Box H is at the left end of the lower shelf, and Box P is on the lower shelf.
- Box D is directly above Box P.
stimuli.solution:
Number the places 1 to 4 from the left on each shelf.
Step 1: J = upper 3, F = lower 3, L = lower 4, B = upper 4.
Step 2: H = lower 1. P is on the lower shelf: the only free place there is 2. D is directly above P: upper 2.
Step 3: N takes the last place, upper 1.

| Shelf | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Upper | N | D | J | B |
| Lower | H | P | F | L |

stimuli.title: Seven boxes of three sizes
stimuli.content:
Seven boxes C, G, M, Q, T, V and Y are kept one above another in a single stack (position 1 is the bottom). Three boxes are Large, two Medium and two Small.

- No box is kept directly on top of a box smaller than itself.
- Box Y is Medium, and Box C is kept immediately below Box Y.
- Box M is kept at the top, and Box T is Small.
- Box G is kept immediately below Box T.
- Box V is kept below Box Q.
stimuli.solution:
Step 1: No box sits on a smaller box, so sizes never increase going up: positions 1–3 are Large, 4–5 Medium and 6–7 Small.
Step 2: M = 7 (Small). T is Small: T = 6, and G, immediately below T, = 5 (Medium).
Step 3: Y is Medium: the only Medium place left is 4, so Y = 4 and C = 3 (Large).
Step 4: V and Q take 1 and 2 with V below: V = 1, Q = 2.

| Position | Box | Size |
|---|---|---|
| 7 | M | Small |
| 6 | T | Small |
| 5 | G | Medium |
| 4 | Y | Medium |
| 3 | C | Large |
| 2 | Q | Large |
| 1 | V | Large |

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Six persons Abha, Babli, Chhotu, Dabbu, Eva and Fanny sit in a straight row, all facing north. (Facing north, the right is towards the east.)
- Only two persons sit to the right of Abha.
- Dabbu sits at the extreme right end, and Chhotu sits between Abha and Dabbu.
- Eva sits at the extreme left end, and Fanny sits immediately to the left of Abha.

Who sits second to the left of Abha?

solution.concept: 'Only two persons to the right' fixes a seat
solution.explanation: With six seats and two persons to her right, Abha is in seat 4. Dabbu = 6, Chhotu = 5, Eva = 1, Fanny = 3, and Babli takes seat 2 — second to Abha's left.
solution.why_others_wrong: Fanny is immediately to her left, Eva third to her left, and Chhotu to her right.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Seven persons Karan, Lekha, Megha, Nikki, Pari, Raju and Sunny sit in a straight row, all facing north. (Facing north, the right is towards the east.)
- Megha sits fourth from the left end, and Raju sits second to the right of Megha.
- Karan sits at the extreme left end and Sunny at the extreme right end.
- Pari sits immediately to the left of Megha.
- Lekha sits to the right of Nikki.

How many persons sit between Karan and Lekha?

solution.concept: Place the fixed seats, then the last pair
solution.explanation: Megha = 4, Raju = 6, Karan = 1, Sunny = 7, Pari = 3. Seats 2 and 5 remain for Nikki and Lekha; Lekha is to the right: Lekha = 5. Between seats 1 and 5 sit Nikki, Pari and Megha: three persons.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: Who faces Kapil?

solution.explanation: Kapil is in Row 1, column 1; facing him is Row 2, column 1: Chanda.
steps: West to east — Row 1 (facing south): Kapil, Arya, Tulsi, Mohan, Gulab, Ravi; Row 2 (facing north): Chanda, Nayan, Dhiren, Hasan, Bhola, Lalit
solution.why_others_wrong: Nayan faces Arya, Lalit faces Ravi and Dhiren faces Tulsi.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: Who sits second to the right of Nayan?

solution.explanation: Nayan is in Row 2, column 2; two seats east is column 4: Hasan.
steps: West to east — Row 1 (facing south): Kapil, Arya, Tulsi, Mohan, Gulab, Ravi; Row 2 (facing north): Chanda, Nayan, Dhiren, Hasan, Bhola, Lalit
solution.why_others_wrong: Dhiren is immediately to his right, Bhola third to his right, and Chanda to his left.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: Who sits immediately to the left of Gulab?

solution.explanation: Gulab is in Row 1, column 5, facing south; his left is east: column 6, Ravi.
steps: West to east — Row 1 (facing south): Kapil, Arya, Tulsi, Mohan, Gulab, Ravi; Row 2 (facing north): Chanda, Nayan, Dhiren, Hasan, Bhola, Lalit
solution.why_others_wrong: Mohan is to his right; Bhola faces him; Lalit is in the other row.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: How many persons sit between Arya and Ravi?

solution.explanation: Arya is in Row 1, column 2 and Ravi in Row 1, column 6: Tulsi, Mohan and Gulab sit between them.
steps: West to east — Row 1 (facing south): Kapil, Arya, Tulsi, Mohan, Gulab, Ravi; Row 2 (facing north): Chanda, Nayan, Dhiren, Hasan, Bhola, Lalit

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: How many vacant seats lie between Bhim and Anvi?

solution.concept: Mark the vacant seats after placing everyone
solution.explanation: Bhim is on seat 1 and Anvi on seat 6; seats 2 and 5 between them are vacant.
steps: Seats 1 to 10 from the left: Bhim, vacant, Esha, Gita, vacant, Anvi, Chiru, vacant, Fuzail, Dolu

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: Who sits third to the left of Fuzail?

solution.explanation: Fuzail is on seat 9; three seats to the left is seat 6: Anvi.
steps: Seats 1 to 10 from the left: Bhim, vacant, Esha, Gita, vacant, Anvi, Chiru, vacant, Fuzail, Dolu
solution.why_others_wrong: Chiru is second to his left (seat 8 is vacant, seat 7 is Chiru's); Gita is further left; Dolu is to his right.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: Which of the following seats is vacant?

solution.explanation: The persons occupy seats 1, 3, 4, 6, 7, 9 and 10, so seats 2, 5 and 8 are vacant.
steps: Seats 1 to 10 from the left: Bhim, vacant, Esha, Gita, vacant, Anvi, Chiru, vacant, Fuzail, Dolu
solution.why_others_wrong: Gita is on seat 4, Chiru on 7 and Esha on 3.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: How many persons sit to the right of Gita?

solution.explanation: Gita is on seat 4; to her right sit Anvi (6), Chiru (7), Fuzail (9) and Dolu (10).
steps: Seats 1 to 10 from the left: Bhim, vacant, Esha, Gita, vacant, Anvi, Chiru, vacant, Fuzail, Dolu

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: Who is the fourth tallest?

solution.concept: Order the last four with the comparison chain
solution.explanation: Kuku, Nanki and Hiran are the three tallest. Of the rest, Ishu is 7th and Rinku is taller than Lado, who is taller than Pammi, so Rinku is 4th.
steps: Left to right (height rank, 1 = tallest): Lado (5), Kuku (1), Mitu (8), Nanki (2), Ishu (7), Hiran (3), Rinku (4), Pammi (6)
solution.why_others_wrong: Lado is 5th, Ishu 7th and Hiran 3rd.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: Among the persons who have two neighbours, how many are taller than both of their neighbours?

solution.concept: Compare each person with both neighbours
solution.explanation: Kuku (taller than Lado and Mitu), Nanki (taller than Mitu and Ishu) and Hiran (taller than Ishu and Rinku) qualify; nobody else does.
steps: Left to right (height rank, 1 = tallest): Lado (5), Kuku (1), Mitu (8), Nanki (2), Ishu (7), Hiran (3), Rinku (4), Pammi (6)

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: Who sits immediately to the left of the second shortest person?

solution.concept: Find the person by rank, then move left
solution.explanation: Ishu is the second shortest and sits on seat 5; seat 4, to the left, is Nanki's.
steps: Left to right (height rank, 1 = tallest): Lado (5), Kuku (1), Mitu (8), Nanki (2), Ishu (7), Hiran (3), Rinku (4), Pammi (6)
solution.why_others_wrong: Hiran is to Ishu's right; Mitu and Kuku are further left.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Six friends Tina, Umesh, Vimla, Waris, Yusuf and Zarna sit around a circular table, equally spaced and all facing the centre. (Facing the centre, the right is anticlockwise and the left clockwise.)
- Umesh sits immediately to the right of Tina, and Yusuf sits opposite Umesh.
- Vimla sits second to the left of Yusuf.
- Zarna does not sit next to Tina.

Who sits immediately to the left of Tina?

solution.concept: Fix one person and go round
solution.explanation: Seats 0 to 5 anticlockwise from Tina: Umesh = 1, Yusuf (opposite) = 4, Vimla (second to Yusuf's left, clockwise) = 2. Seats 3 and 5 remain; seat 5 is next to Tina, so Zarna = 3 and Waris = 5. Tina's left (clockwise) neighbour is seat 5: Waris.
steps: Zarna not next to Tina ⇒ Zarna 3, Waris 5
solution.why_others_wrong: Umesh is on Tina's right; Zarna and Yusuf are not her neighbours.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: Who sits opposite Rupal?

solution.explanation: Rupal is on chair 1; chair 6 is opposite: Ujjal.
steps: Chairs anticlockwise from Ajay: Ajay, Rupal, vacant, Fateh, Bimal, Jassi, Ujjal, vacant, Disha, Lucky
solution.why_others_wrong: Jassi is opposite Ajay, Bimal is opposite Lucky, and Disha is opposite Fateh.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: Who sits second to the left of Fateh?

solution.concept: Count the vacant chair as well
solution.explanation: Fateh is on chair 3; his left is clockwise: chair 2 (vacant), then chair 1, Rupal.
steps: Chairs anticlockwise from Ajay: Ajay, Rupal, vacant, Fateh, Bimal, Jassi, Ujjal, vacant, Disha, Lucky
solution.why_others_wrong: Ajay is third to his left, Bimal is to his right, and Lucky is further clockwise.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: How many persons sit between Ajay and Bimal, counting from Ajay's right?

solution.explanation: From Ajay (0) anticlockwise: Rupal (1), vacant (2), Fateh (3), then Bimal (4). Two persons sit between them.
steps: Chairs anticlockwise from Ajay: Ajay, Rupal, vacant, Fateh, Bimal, Jassi, Ujjal, vacant, Disha, Lucky

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: Who sits immediately to the right of the vacant chair that is next to Ujjal?

solution.concept: A vacant chair has a 'right' as seen by a person facing the centre from it
solution.explanation: The vacant chair next to Ujjal is chair 7. Facing the centre from it, the right is anticlockwise: chair 8, Disha.
steps: Chairs anticlockwise from Ajay: Ajay, Rupal, vacant, Fateh, Bimal, Jassi, Ujjal, vacant, Disha, Lucky

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Eight persons Ambar, Chitti, Dhruva, Garima, Hoshang, Jalaj, Mukta and Navami sit around a circular table, equally spaced. Some face the centre and the others face outside, and every person sits exactly opposite a person who faces the other way. (Facing the centre, the right is anticlockwise; facing outside, it is clockwise.)
- Ambar faces the centre, and Dhruva sits opposite Ambar.
- Garima faces outside and sits immediately to the right of Ambar.
- Jalaj sits immediately to the left of Garima, and Mukta sits opposite Garima.
- Hoshang sits second to the left of Dhruva, and Chitti sits immediately to the left of Ambar.
- Chitti faces outside, and Jalaj and Navami face the same direction.

Who sits second to the right of Navami?

solution.concept: Opposite persons face opposite ways — use this to fix facings
solution.explanation: Seats 0 to 7 anticlockwise from Ambar (centre): Dhruva 4 faces outside (opposite Ambar). Garima (outside) = 1, so Mukta (opposite) = 5 faces the centre. Garima's left is anticlockwise: Jalaj = 2. Dhruva faces outside, so his left is anticlockwise: Hoshang = 6. Chitti, on Ambar's left (clockwise), = 7 and faces outside, so Navami (3, opposite Chitti) faces the centre, and Jalaj faces the centre like Navami (and Hoshang, opposite Jalaj, faces outside). Navami faces the centre, so second to her right (anticlockwise) is seat 5: Mukta.
steps: Chitti O ⇒ Navami C ⇒ Jalaj C ⇒ Hoshang O
solution.why_others_wrong: Dhruva is immediately to her right; Hoshang third to her right; Garima is to her left.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Some boxes are kept one above another in a single stack. The number of boxes is not given; R, S and T are three of them.
- Box R is kept sixth from the top, and Box S is kept fourth from the bottom.
- Exactly two boxes are kept between Box R and Box S.
- The stack has more than eight boxes, and Box T is kept immediately above Box R.

How many boxes are kept above Box T?

solution.concept: Test both orders of R and S; keep the one the size condition allows
solution.explanation: S is 4th from the bottom. If R were below S it would be 1st from the bottom and also 6th from the top, giving only 6 boxes — not more than eight. So R is 4 + 3 = 7th from the bottom, and the stack has 7 + 6 − 1 = 12 boxes. T is 8th from the bottom, so 12 − 8 = 4 boxes are above it.
steps: R below S ⇒ R 1st from bottom ⇒ 6 boxes ✗
R above S ⇒ R 7th from bottom ⇒ n = 12

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Six boxes D, F, L, P, U and Z are kept one above another in a single stack (position 1 is the bottom and 6 the top). Their weights are 5, 10, 15, 20, 25 and 30 kg, one weight per box.
- Box Z is the heaviest box, and the boxes kept above Z weigh 40 kg in all.
- Box D is the lightest box and is kept immediately above Box Z.
- The two boxes kept below Box Z weigh 35 kg in all.
- Box U is at the top, and Box P is kept immediately below Box U.
- Box F is kept below Box L.
- Box U is lighter than Box P but heavier than Box L.

What is the weight of Box F?

solution.concept: Split the total weight around the heaviest box
solution.explanation: The weights total 105 kg. Z (30 kg) has 40 kg above it and 35 kg below it, and exactly two boxes below it, so Z = 3. D (5 kg) = 4, U = 6, P = 5, and F, L take 1, 2 with F below. The two bottom boxes weigh 35 kg: 10 + 25 or 15 + 20. P and U weigh 40 − 5 = 35 kg: the other pair. U is lighter than P and heavier than L. If F, L are 10 and 25, then P, U are 20 and 15, and L must be 10 (lighter than U): F = 25. If F, L were 15 and 20, U would be 10 and could not be heavier than L. So F weighs 25 kg.
steps: F + L = 35 and P + U = 35: {10, 25} and {15, 20} in some order
